chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “It was said to Malak al-Mawt عليه السلام, ‘How do you seize the souls while some of them are in the west and some of them are in the east in a single hour?’ So he said, ‘I call them, and they answer me.’”

He said: “Then Malak al-Mawt عليه السلام said: ‘Indeed, the world before my hands is like a bowl before the hands of one of you, from which he takes whatever he wishes; and the world to me is like a dirham in the palm of one of you, turning it however he wishes.’”

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly realm in its entirety
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمِ: a coin, used as a comparison for control and ease of turning
key_terms.الْأَرْوَاحَ: the souls of human beings at the time of death
key_terms.الْقَصْعَةِ: a bowl or large dish, used as a comparison for ease of access
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the eastern region, mentioned to indicate distance
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the western region, mentioned to indicate distance
key_terms.مَلَكِ الْمَوْتِ: the Angel of Death entrusted with taking souls

ai.seo_question: How does Malak al-Mawt seize souls in different places at the same time?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the vast reach and ease with which Malak al-Mawt عليه السلام carries out the taking of souls across the world. It emphasizes the unseen power granted by Allah to His angel and presents death as occurring under divine command without limitation of distance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.354 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said: "It was said to the Angel of Death (as), 'How do you seize souls while some are in the west and others in the east at the same moment?'
He said: 'I summon them, and they respond to me.'

Imam (as) said: “Then, The Angel of Death, said: 'The world is like a bowl in front of me from which I take as I please, and the world is like a coin in the palm of one of you, which you turn as you wish.'
